author: Ian Young
title: Kentuckians feeling pain at the pump as Iran war continues - NewsBreak
text:
By Ian Young ,
1 hours ago OWENSBORO, Ky. (WEHT) — Congressman Brett Guthrie was in western Kentucky and stopped by Apollo High School to celebrate students competing in the Congressional App challenge.
The program recognizes students who design and build their own apps. While there we also talked with him about gas prices.
Right now, prices are at a 4-year high as tensions with Iran continue to impact the market. Guthrie says President Trump has announced that a deal with Iran is in the works.
He tells us he understands the importance of affordable gas for Kentuckians, but says the president is right and Iran cannot have nuclear weapons.
“I certainly don’t dismiss the pain that it’s caused the American people, but I think it’s going to be the right thing when we have Iran without access to a nuclear weapon,” says Guthrie.
On Wednesday, Governor Andy Beshear announced he’s signing an emergency regulation to freeze the gas tax. It goes into effect July 1.
